nodes.label: DocxGenerator
nodes.rationale: Creates a blank docx.Document() and applies CategoryConfig.formatting (margins, styles) while hardcoding many sizes/colors; accepts a template_path it never uses.

nodes.label: DOCX/PDF Formatting Divergence
nodes.rationale: Because only DocxGenerator reads CategoryConfig.formatting while report.tex.j2 hardcodes font, size, margins and spacing, changing YAML changes the DOCX only and changing the template changes the PDF only - the two outputs silently diverge.

nodes.label: FrontPage
nodes.rationale: Carries institution/university/campus/department, document type, title, subtitle, course, submitted-by/to, date, logo path; the LaTeX title page hardcodes 'Institute of Engineering' instead of front_page.institution and ignores program/semester/section.

nodes.label: LatexGenerator
nodes.rationale: Converts Markdown to LaTeX and renders the Jinja2 template with LaTeX-safe delimiters, but deliberately takes only report and output_path - it does not accept CategoryConfig, so YAML formatting never reaches the PDF.

nodes.label: Markdown Conversion Rules
nodes.rationale: Supports headings, bold/italic/code, lists, quotes, rules, and tables, but no math, no images, no links, no nested lists; math is escaped to literal text because sanitize_math is unused. A separate parser exists for DOCX, so the same body renders differently per format.

nodes.label: PDF Engine Fallback Chain (Tectonic to XeLaTeX to LibreOffice)
nodes.norm_label: pdf engine fallback chain (tectonic to xelatex to libreoffice)
nodes.rationale: Engine order is hardcoded Tectonic then XeLaTeX/pdflatex then LibreOffice; settings.pdf_engine and pdf_fallback_engine are never read, and metadata.json labels any successful PDF as tectonic/xelatex even when LibreOffice produced it.

nodes.label: PdfExporter
nodes.rationale: Best-quality-first fallback chain: Tectonic → XeLaTeX → LibreOffice, storing the PDF next to the DOCX. The chain exists so a missing engine degrades gracefully while DOCX remains available.

nodes.label: ReportContent
nodes.rationale: The single content contract both renderers consume; adding a field here does not render it automatically, which is the root of several divergence bugs.

nodes.label: Fabricated Default References
nodes.rationale: Two invented citations are inserted whenever none are supplied. Treated as an academic-integrity and trust problem rather than cosmetic, because the evaluator never checks reference authenticity; fix is to fail or emit [[MISSING: references]].

nodes.label: P0 Defects Backlog
nodes.rationale: P0 is defined as breaking a user-visible path or producing incorrect output; the six P0 items are SourceType import, OCR fitz bug, preference injection, ignored PDF engine setting, fabricated references, and evaluator fail-open.

nodes.label: PDF Engine Setting Ignored
nodes.rationale: settings.pdf_engine and pdf_fallback_engine are editable in the UI but pdf_exporter hardcodes the order, so the user's choice has no effect and a machine without Tectonic still tries it first.

nodes.label: Persisted Preferences Never Injected into Workflow
nodes.norm_label: persisted preferences never injected into workflow
nodes.rationale: Described as the single highest-impact product defect: the generator reads normalized.metadata['student_profile'] but nothing writes it, so saved Settings/Profile values never reach the front page.

nodes.label: Phased Implementation Roadmap (Phases 0-6)
nodes.rationale: Ordering is dependency-driven: correctness first (Phase 0), then trust/evaluation (Phase 1), then unified output (Phase 2), preferences UI (Phase 3), AI quality and observability (Phase 4), persistence/operations (Phase 5), polish (Phase 6). Each phase carries acceptance criteria rather than task lists alone.

nodes.label: Layered Testing Strategy (unit, integration, UI, AI regression, document regression)
nodes.norm_label: layered testing strategy (unit, integration, ui, ai regression, document regression)
nodes.rationale: Golden prompt rendering, schema conformance, evaluator behavior on a fixed failing report, and PDF text-extraction assertions are proposed because the highest-risk paths (real provider, PDF compilation, preference injection, fail-open, EDIT routing) are currently untested.

nodes.label: IOE Color Palette (ioeblue, ioegold, textgray, linkblue)
nodes.norm_label: ioe color palette (ioeblue, ioegold, textgray, linkblue)
nodes.rationale: ioeblue RGB(27,54,93) approximates the DOCX navy 0x1B365D, but the values are duplicated constants rather than shared configuration.

nodes.label: IOE Pulchowk Academic Report LaTeX Template
nodes.norm_label: ioe pulchowk academic report latex template
nodes.rationale: This template is the authoritative visual identity of the PDF, so all presentation rules hardcoded here (12pt, a4paper, Times New Roman, 1.25in left margin, 1.25 stretch) override the YAML formatting config and are the source of DOCX/PDF divergence.

nodes.label: Manual thebibliography Block
nodes.rationale: Uses loop.index for bibitem labels and ignores Citation.key, so a [1] in the body matches the first item only by coincidence; no BibTeX, no IEEE enforcement, no DOI/URL rendering.

nodes.label: LaTeX Title Page Block
nodes.rationale: Builds logo, university hierarchy, gold rule, document type, title, submitted-by/submitted-to minipages and date; the line 'Institute of Engineering' is literal rather than front_page.institution, which is a known P1 defect.

nodes.label: Tribhuvan University (T.U.) Logo Crest
nodes.rationale: A circular crest: navy blue ring with a gold outer border, a white interior containing a stylized open book/monument form with a gold chevron above it, and the letters 'T.U.' in white serif capitals on a navy band at the bottom. It is the Tribhuvan University emblem used as the front-page institutional logo in both the DOCX and LaTeX outputs via FrontPage.logo_path.

nodes.label: Split Composition Root
nodes.rationale: There is no DI container; dependencies are passed explicitly, but the composition root is split across app/main.py, app/ui/workers.py and workflow/graph.py rather than centralized.

nodes.label: RagRetriever / ChromaDB Retrieval
nodes.rationale: Optional grounding in course material: chunk 1000/150 overlap, embed, store in a local ChromaDB collection, retrieve top-k. Disabled by default in all three category configs, so the default path is a no-op.

nodes.label: Evaluator
nodes.rationale: Deterministic checks (required sections, word limits, banned phrases, citation keys) run before per-section semantic evaluation. Known limitations: hardcoded overall_score, incomplete deterministic checks, fail-open on exception, no calibration set.

nodes.label: Evaluator Fails Open
nodes.rationale: Any provider exception marks the section passed with score 0.9, so an outage or schema mismatch shows a false green state on the human review page. Fix is fail-closed or a distinct unverified state.

nodes.label: Assignment Evaluation Prompt
nodes.rationale: Defines a three-state verdict (passed/failed/inconclusive) rather than a boolean, which is what makes an explicit 'not evaluated' state representable - though the evaluator code does not currently honor it on exception.

nodes.label: Final Lab Evaluation Prompt
nodes.rationale: Peer-review framing over clarity, scientific methodology, experimental data fidelity, and error analysis - the strictest rubric of the three categories.

nodes.label: Initial Lab Evaluation Prompt
nodes.rationale: Focuses the rubric on scientific accuracy and checks that calculations, procedure steps, and observations match the experimental requirements without hallucination.

nodes.label: Data-driven YAML Category Rules
nodes.rationale: Academic rules (required sections, word limits, formatting, rubric weights, prompt paths, RAG switches, reference rules) live in YAML so adding a category or tweaking a rubric is a configuration change, not a code change. This is the primary extension point.

nodes.label: Eleven-Step Workflow Pipeline
nodes.rationale: The spine of the app: normalise → classify → load config → check missing info → retrieve references → generate → evaluate → regenerate failed → human review → export → persist. Two gates are deliberate: missing information and human approval.

nodes.label: Two Interrupt Pause Points
nodes.rationale: There are exactly two LangGraph interrupts (check_missing_info and human_review), one bounded evaluation→regeneration loop, and export is reachable only through the human decision.

nodes.label: Mandatory Human Approval Gate
nodes.rationale: Nothing leaves the machine without a human: export is unreachable until the review node records an approval, and the gate is a structural property of the graph, not a UI convention.

nodes.label: LangGraph State Machine Orchestration
nodes.rationale: The process has loops (evaluate → regenerate), two pause points (missing information, human review) and must survive a crash. LangGraph gives an explicit resumable state machine instead of free-form agents, and SQLite checkpoints make every step resumable.

nodes.label: Local-first Single-user Desktop Application
nodes.rationale: The product is a single-user local desktop app for students: the student signs in with their own Google account, data lives on their machine, and there is no HTTP server. 'Backend' means the in-process service/orchestration layer, not a network service.

nodes.label: State-Machine Orchestrator Architectural Style
nodes.rationale: The key decision is that the LLM never controls the flow: fixed nodes and deterministic conditional edges, with the LLM only producing typed payloads inside nodes. This is what allows crash resume, data/review pauses, and per-section retry.

nodes.label: Classifier
nodes.rationale: Rule keywords resolve most cases deterministically (final_lab 0.90, initial_lab 0.88, assignment 0.85) and only fall back to an LLM ClassificationResult when no rule matches; manual selection bypasses all of it with confidence 1.0.

nodes.label: GeminiProvider
nodes.rationale: Uses google.genai.Client with v1beta, 60s timeout, JSON response mime type, Pydantic response_schema, and a hardcoded model fallback list [primary, fallback, gemini-2.5-flash, gemini-2.5-flash-lite] to survive model unavailability.

nodes.label: MockProvider
nodes.rationale: Deterministic offline provider with keyword classification, sample section body, force_pass evaluation, and SHA-256-derived 768-dim pseudo-embeddings. Excellent for unit tests and offline demos, but RAG evaluations run against it measure plumbing, not retrieval quality.

nodes.label: Model Configuration Drift
nodes.rationale: Settings defaults, .env.example, UI choices, and the hardcoded Gemini fallback list are not derived from one source of truth, so model names disagree across the app; GEMINI_PRO_MODEL is declared but unused.

nodes.label: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
nodes.rationale: ChromaDB collection per course with 1000-char/150-overlap character chunking. Disabled in all category configs and indexed with MockProvider pseudo-embeddings, so retrieval quality is currently meaningless.

nodes.label: NVIDIA Embedding Compatibility and Reindex Requirement
nodes.norm_label: nvidia embedding compatibility and reindex requirement
nodes.rationale: nemotron-3.5-embed-1b requires input_type passage for indexing and query for retrieval; using the wrong mode materially reduces accuracy. Migration is safe because RAG is disabled, but enabling it later needs a one-time reindex rather than a schema change.

nodes.label: NVIDIA NIM Model Selection (Lightning primary, Bolt fallback)
nodes.norm_label: nvidia nim model selection (lightning primary, bolt fallback)
nodes.rationale: Lightning (30B/3B active, 1M context) is primary because it is production-intended, covers the 100k-char cap plus prompts, and has the strongest reasoning; Bolt (8B/4B, 65,536 context) is fallback because it has the most reliable documented json_schema structured-output path.

nodes.label: NvidiaProvider
nodes.rationale: Planned ai/llm/nvidia.py implementing LLMProvider over the OpenAI-compatible NIM endpoint, with lazy openai import so offline mode and imports survive a missing package, max_retries=0 because the provider owns fallback, and no hardcoded model IDs.

nodes.label: build_llm_provider Provider Factory
nodes.rationale: A single selection point returning MockProvider when use_mock or no key is set, otherwise NvidiaProvider; introduced to remove duplicated selection logic and keep RAG indexing on the same embedding model as retrieval.

nodes.label: NIM Structured Output Strategy
nodes.rationale: Tries native response_format json_schema with strict=True first, falls back to a JSON-only instruction plus schema text when the endpoint rejects it, then makes one repair request containing the validation error; this keeps the native fast path for Bolt while giving Lightning a documented path.

nodes.label: Tenacity (Declared but Unused)
nodes.rationale: Tenacity is declared as a core dependency but zero imports exist; retry behaviour is hand-written in workflow/routing.py and the Gemini provider.

nodes.label: Fabricated Placeholder References (Academic-Integrity Risk)
nodes.rationale: When no references are supplied, the generator inserts two fabricated placeholder citations that are rendered as if real. This is an academic-integrity risk even if intended as scaffolding.

nodes.label: OCR Fallback (Currently Broken)
nodes.rationale: Scanned PDFs have no text layer, so the parser rasterises pages and runs Tesseract. A runtime defect (fitz.Matrix referenced without importing fitz) means the OCR branch silently never produces text.

nodes.label: Deterministic Python / LLM Division of Labour
nodes.norm_label: deterministic python / llm division of labour
nodes.rationale: Deterministic Python does everything it can compute or validate exactly (word counts, required sections, arithmetic, LaTeX escaping, parsing, formatting); the LLM is used only where language understanding is genuinely needed (classification, drafting, rubric judgement). This avoids hallucinated data and unformatted output.

nodes.label: Preference Injection Gap
nodes.rationale: Student profile and document preferences are persisted but never injected into generation, so the front page falls back to 'Student' and hardcoded institution defaults.

nodes.label: Prompt Architecture
nodes.rationale: System/generation/evaluation prompt triplets per category, rendered with Jinja2 from a fixed variable set. Generation prompts are intentionally short and rely on the system prompt plus the schema; system prompts carry the anti-hallucination rules and [[MISSING: ...]] instructions.

nodes.label: SectionGenerator
nodes.rationale: Generates sections sequentially, each with only a heading+word-count summary of prior sections rather than their full text; this limits context growth but also limits cross-section coherence.

nodes.label: Untrusted-Data Wrapping and Sanitization
nodes.rationale: sanitize_external_input caps length at 100k chars and redacts known injection phrases; wrap_untrusted_data wraps text in a random 16-hex boundary. Generator and classifier use it, but the evaluator does not - a prompt-injection gap.

nodes.label: Assignment Generation Prompt
nodes.rationale: Instructs the model to cite only supplied references, never invent bibliographic data, and use [[MISSING: source]] when no reference material exists; the user_provided_data block is explicitly framed as non-authoritative context.

nodes.label: Final Lab Generation Prompt
nodes.rationale: Frames the section as part of a comprehensive laboratory report and supplies theory/source data plus calculation summaries; the doc notes it asks for IEEE style that neither the evaluator nor the renderer enforces.

nodes.label: Initial Lab Generation Prompt
nodes.rationale: Adds calculated_data and an explicit structured output format (Markdown body, tables, citations) on top of the shared reference-citation rules.

nodes.label: Deterministic-First Design Principle
nodes.rationale: The LLM is used only for classification, drafting, and rubric evaluation; everything computable or validatable deterministically (normalization, hashing, word counts, required-section checks, arithmetic, LaTeX escaping, parsing, layout) is done in Python. Chosen because it reduces cost, variance, and hallucination surface for a document-generation product.

nodes.label: LangGraph SQLite Checkpointer
nodes.rationale: A separate storage/workflow_checkpoints.db via SqliteSaver is what makes interrupt/resume and crash recovery work; one connection per get_checkpointer() call.

nodes.label: Domain Contracts (RawInput, NormalizedInput, ReportContent, HumanDecision, EvaluationResult)
nodes.norm_label: domain contracts (rawinput, normalizedinput, reportcontent, humandecision, evaluationresult)
nodes.rationale: Pydantic models are the only cross-layer contract in a single-process desktop app with no HTTP API; they also validate every LLM structured output.

nodes.label: Qt Signal Contracts
nodes.rationale: Substitutes for an HTTP API: pages emit start_generation/review_decided/open_* and the worker emits progress/interrupt/finished/error signals, keeping the workflow off the UI thread.

nodes.label: WorkflowState
nodes.rationale: A TypedDict with total=False that is the de facto internal API between workflow nodes; errors is declared but never populated and references is unused by nodes.

nodes.label: Mental Model: The Graph Is the Application
nodes.norm_label: mental model: the graph is the application
nodes.rationale: Three ideas are said to unlock the codebase: the LangGraph graph is the application (UI only starts/resumes it and renders interrupts), Pydantic models are the contracts, and there are two independent renderers that can diverge.

nodes.label: Repositories (Assignment, WorkflowRun, Document, AuditLog)
nodes.rationale: Each repository commits inside its methods with no unit-of-work, so persist_node's three writes are three independent transactions and a mid-way failure leaves partial history. Migrations only bump schema_versions - a placeholder, not a framework.

nodes.label: SQLite Schema (assignments, workflow_runs, generated_documents, audit_logs, reference_documents)
nodes.norm_label: sqlite schema (assignments, workflow_runs, generated_documents, audit_logs, reference_documents)
nodes.rationale: SQLModel over SQLite with WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, foreign_keys=ON; source_records and workflow_runs exist but are never written by the workflow, and there are no FK cascade rules.
